facts.statement: Styxosaurus fossils are mainly found in the Niobrara and Pierre Shale formations in North America.
facts.quote: Fossils are known from North America and are mainly found in the Niobrara and Pierre Shale formations.

facts.statement: The genus name Styxosaurus honors the mythological River Styx, which separated the Greek underworld from the world of the living.
facts.quote: Styxosaurus fue nombrado por el mítico río Estigia (Στυξ, styx), el cual separaba al inframundo griego del mundo de los vivos.

facts.statement: The holotype of Styxosaurus snowii consists of a complete skull and 20 vertebrae, first described by S.W. Williston.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Styxosaurus snowii a complete skull and 20 vertebrae and was first described by S.W. Williston

facts.statement: The genus Styxosaurus was coined by Samuel Paul Welles in 1943 based on a type specimen found on Hell Creek in Logan County, Kansas.
facts.quote: The type specimen was found on Hell Creek in Logan County, Kansas, which is the source of the genus name coined by Samuel Paul Welles, who described the genus in 1943.

facts.statement: A more complete specimen of Styxosaurus, SDSMT 451, was discovered near Iona, South Dakota, in 1945.
facts.quote: Another more complete specimen, SDSMT 451, was discovered near Iona, South Dakota, also in the US, in 1945.

facts.statement: In 2023, Smith and O'Keefe named the species Styxosaurus rezaci based on a specimen from the Cenomanian of Nebraska.
facts.quote: In 2023, another species of Styxosaurus, S. rezaci, was named by Smith and O'Keefe, based on a specimen from the Cenomanian of Nebraska previously thought to belong to Thalassomedon.

facts.statement: Specimen NJSM 15435 of Styxosaurus snowii was reported to measure 10 meters, though it lacks the skull and frontmost neck vertebrae.
facts.quote: The S. snowii specimen NJSM 15435 was reported to measure 10 m, though it lacks the skull and the frontmost neck vertebrae.

facts.statement: Specimen SDSM 451 is estimated to be around 11.3 meters in body length and 3.1 metric tons in body mass.
facts.quote: The size of specimen SDSM 451 assigned to Styxosaurus sp. is estimated around 11.3 m in body length and 3.1 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: The holotype cranium measures 42 cm in length, while the mandible measures 48 cm in length.
facts.quote: The cranium of the holotype measures 42 cm long, with its mandible measuring 48 cm long.

facts.statement: Styxosaurus had sharp, conical teeth adapted for puncturing and holding prey, and it swallowed its food whole.
facts.quote: Its sharp teeth were conical and were adapted to puncture and hold rather than to cut; like other plesiosaurs, Styxosaurus swallowed its food whole.

facts.statement: While ballast is possible, a Styxosaurus specimen from western Kansas contained ground-up fish bones mixed with gastroliths, suggesting a digestive function.
facts.quote: Although it is possible Styxosaurus may have used the stones as ballast, a Styxosaurus specimen found in the Pierre Shale of western Kansas included ground up fish bones mixed with the gastroliths.

facts.statement: It is likely that elasmosaurs, including Styxosaurus, used gastroliths as a gastric mill to grind food.
facts.quote: it appears likely that elasmosaurs used them as a gastric mill.

facts.statement: Styxosaurus probably fed on belemnites, fish, and squid.
facts.quote: Styxosaurus, like most other plesiosaurs, probably fed on belemnites, fish (Gillicus, etc.) and squid.

facts.statement: Styxosaurus snowii belongs to the group of elasmosaurs and is closely related to Elasmosaurus platyurus.
facts.quote: Styxosaurus snowii is from a group called elasmosaurs, and is closely related to Elasmosaurus platyurus, which was found in Kansas, USA, in 1867.

facts.statement: The first described Styxosaurus was initially named Cimoliasaurus snowii by S.W. Williston in 1890.
facts.quote: The first Styxosaurus to be described was initially called Cimoliasaurus snowii by S.W. Williston in 1890.

facts.statement: The name was changed from Cimoliasaurus snowii to Elasmosaurus snowii in 1906, and finally to Styxosaurus snowii by Welles in 1943.
facts.quote: The name was later changed to Elasmosaurus snowii by Williston in 1906 and then to Styxosaurus snowii by Welles in 1943.

facts.statement: Styxosaurus is classified within the family Elasmosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Elasmosauridae

facts.statement: Styxosaurus belongs to the subfamily Elasmosaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Elasmosaurinae

facts.statement: The genus authority for Styxosaurus is attributed to Welles & Bump in 1949.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Welles & Bump, 1949

facts.statement: Styxosaurus lived in the Late Cretaceous (approximately 85.8 to 71 million years ago, from the Santonian to Campanian stages) in what is now the United States.
facts.quote: Styxosaurus es un género extinto representado por una única especie de plesiosauroide elasmosáurido que vivió en el Cretácico Superior (hace aproximadamente 85,8 y 71 millones de años, desde el Santoniense hasta el Campaniense), en lo que es Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: Styxosaurus belongs to the elasmosaurid group and is closely related to Elasmosaurus platyurus.
facts.quote: Styxosaurus snowii forma parte del grupo de los elasmosáuridos, y es un pariente cercano de Elasmosaurus platyurus

facts.statement: The holotype specimen included a complete skull and more than 20 cervical vertebrae found near Hell Creek in Kansas by Judge E.P. West.
facts.quote: El espécimen incluía un cráneo completo y más de 20 vértebras cervicales (KUVP 1301) que fueron halladas cerca de Hell Creek en Kansas por Judge E.P. West

facts.statement: The name was changed to Elasmosaurus snowii by Williston in 1906 and later to Styxosaurus snowii by Welles in 1943.
facts.quote: El nombre fue luego cambiado a Elasmosaurus snowii por Williston en 1906 y luego a Styxosaurus snowii por Welles en 1943

facts.statement: A second species, Styxosaurus browni, was named by Welles in 1952 but is now considered a modern synonym of Hydralmosaurus serpentinus.
facts.quote: Una segunda especie, Styxosaurus browni, fue nombrada por Welles en 1952. Sin embargo, más tarde este se ha vuelto un sinónimo más moderno de Hydralmosaurus serpentinus

facts.statement: Styxosaurus was a large plesiosaur, one of several elasmosaurid species that appeared in the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Styxosaurus era un plesiosaurio grande, una de varias especies de elasmosáuridos que aparecieron en el Cretácico Superior

facts.statement: In elasmosaurids, the neck typically comprises at least half the body length and is composed of between 60 and 72 vertebrae.
facts.quote: En estos el cuello típicamente comprende al menos la mitad de longitud del cuerpo, y está compuesto por entre 60 a 72 vértebras

facts.statement: Its conical teeth were designed to pierce and hold rather than cut, so Styxosaurus swallowed its food whole like other plesiosaurs.
facts.quote: Sus dientes eran cónicos y estaban diseñados para atravesar y sostener más que para cortar, por lo que, como otros plesiosaurios, Styxosaurus tragaría su comida entera

facts.statement: Like many other plesiosaurs, Styxosaurus probably fed on belemnites, fish such as Gillicus, and squids.
facts.quote: Styxosaurus, como muchos otros plesiosaurios, probablemente se alimentaba de belemnites, peces (como Gillicus) y calamares

facts.statement: With its interlocking teeth, Styxosaurus could catch slippery prey before swallowing it.
facts.quote: Con sus dientes entrelazados, Styxosaurus podía atrapar a presas resbaladizas antes de ingerirlas

facts.statement: Styxosaurus lived from the Coniacian to the Campanian stages, between 89.8 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Campanian (89.8 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Styxosaurus is Elasmosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Elasmosaurinae

facts.statement: Styxosaurus belongs to the family Elasmosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Elasmosauridae

facts.statement: Styxosaurus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Styxosaurus is Styxosaurus snowii.
facts.quote: Type species: Styxosaurus snowii
